messages.text: Antonelli fastest from Verstappen ahead of qualifying in Malaysia

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to set up a Mercedes versus Red Bull fight for pole position.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Kimi Antonelli fastest from Max Verstappen ahead of qualifying at Sepang International Circuit | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Kimi Antonelli fastest from Max Verstappen ahead of qualifying at Sepang International Circuit Championship leader Kimi Antonelli topped final practice in Malaysia from Max Verstappen; watch Qualifying later on Saturday at 9am with the race itself on Sunday at 8am (build-up from 6.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event By Nigel Chiu in Sepang Saturday 3 October 2026 07:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A mystery object brings out the red flag and stops final practice at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to set up a Mercedes versus Red Bull fight for pole position. Antonelli, who leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, struggled on Friday but was 0.278s quicker than Verstappen. Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar took third ahead of Russell fourth but both drivers were more than half a second behind Antonelli, who appears to have found a nice rhythm in time for qualifying later on Saturday at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 , at the Sepang International Circuit. metadata.content: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Scandinavia seeks sixth Group 1 in Prix du Cadran | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Today on Sky Sports Racing: Scandinavia seeks sixth Group 1 in Prix du Cadran Arc weekend gets under way at ParisLongchamp on Saturday with Gold Cup hero Scandinavia looking well-placed to land the Prix du Cadran; Ascot plays host to domestic action with Thunder Call and Mezcala in the feature contest Thursday 1 October 2026 18:30, UK Image: Scandinavia headlines the Prix du Cadran Scandinavia takes on Queenstown and Caballo De Mar as Arc weekend gets underway - live on Sky Sports Racing . 4.00 ParisLongchamp - Star stayer Scandinavia bids for a sixth Group 1 success Superstar stayer Scandinavia is the headline act on Day 1 of the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe meeting. Aidan O'Brien's prolific winner heads a field of 10 for this Prix du Cadran . He arrives unbeaten in his past eight starts recording a staggering five Group 1 wins in the process and looks hard to oppose as he heads up in distance once again. Stablemate Queenstown , the ride of Wayne Lordan, heads the likely dangers. He returned with an excellent victory in Group 3 company at the Curragh in August before chasing home Scandinavia in the Irish St Leger. Davison has the unique distinction of having trained both Joshua and Fury. The trainer, who has also coached Fabio Wardley and Moses Itauma among others, helped Fury in his comeback from a long hiatus from the sport, an unbeaten run that included his first fight with Deontay Wilder in 2018. More recently Davison has worked with Joshua, though AJ left and brought in trainers from Oleksandr Usyk's camp for his last two fights. messages.text: Wade and Aspinall make statement ahead of World Grand Prix semi-finals

metadata.summary: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall put in statement performances that will have made their semi-final opponents take note ahead of a mouthwatering Saturday night line-up at the World Grand Prix.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall with statement displays ahead of semi-finals | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall with statement displays ahead of semi-finals James Wade faces Luke Humphries in final four after dropping just one leg in win over Gian van Veen; Nathan Aspinall averages 105.15 to set up Gerwyn Price meeting; watch the World Grand Prix semi-finals live on Saturday, from 8pm on Sky Sports+, 8.30pm on Main Event Saturday 3 October 2026 07:29, UK Image: James Wade will face Luke Humphries in the semi-finals of the World Grand Prix on Saturday James Wade and Nathan Aspinall put in statement performances that will have made their semi-final opponents take note ahead of a mouthwatering Saturday night line-up at the World Grand Prix. Aspinall threatened to set a new tournament record average when storming to a 3-0 win over Ryan Joyce, his 105.15 mark ultimately landing as the fourth-highest in history and the best-ever in a quarter-final. Wade, meanwhile, dropped only one leg as he, in his words, "bashed up" world No 2 Gian van Veen in a match that lasted little more than 20 minutes. messages.text: Kim gains exemption from mandatory military service after Asian Games gold

metadata.summary: Tom Kim secured an exemption from completing full mandatory military service in South Korea after he clinched gold in the Men's Individual Strokeplay event at the Asian Games.
metadata.content: Tom Kim gains exemption from South Korea’s military service after securing Asian Games gold medal | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tom Kim gains exemption from South Korea’s military service after securing Asian Games gold medal Tom Kim claimed a three-shot victory in the Men's Individual Strokeplay event to secure gold at the Asian Games and exempt him from completing full mandatory military service; watch Kim in action throughout the PGA Tour season, live on Sky Sports Saturday 3 October 2026 09:01, UK Image: South Korea's Tom Kim secured gold at the Asian Games on Saturday Tom Kim secured an exemption from completing full mandatory military service in South Korea after he clinched gold in the Men's Individual Strokeplay event at the Asian Games. The 24-year-old took a one-shot lead heading into the final round, but carded a sensational six-under 64 to secure gold and finish three shots clear of Japan's Higa Kazuki, China's Wenyi Ding and Sadom Kaewkanjana of Thailand. Kim top-scored for the International Team at last week's Presidents Cup against Team USA before making an immediate trip to Japan, where he was among three South Korean male golfers to feature at Kasugai Country Club. messages.text: Man City sponsor's 2015 statement raises questions about appeal strategy

metadata.summary: Manchester City’s strategy in their bid to clear their name after being found guilty of breaking more than 100 of the Premier League's rules has been brought into question by a statement their main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to the US government in 2015.
metadata.content: Man City appeal: Club's strategy brought into question by 2015 statement main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to US government | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City appeal: Club's strategy brought into question by 2015 statement main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to US government Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City deny all charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023 By Zinny Boswell and Kaveh Solhekol Friday 2 October 2026 23:00, UK Manchester City’s strategy in their bid to clear their name after being found guilty of breaking more than 100 of the Premier League's rules has been brought into question by a statement their main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to the US government in 2015. Sky Sports News understands that City are expected to argue as part of their appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's majority owners, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG). However, a statement Etihad submitted to the US Departments of Commerce, Transportation and State in May 2015 appears to contradict this explanation. messages.text: Djokovic battles through fitness issues to produce resilient China Open comeback

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic again appeared to struggle with fitness issues as he came from behind to avoid a second-round exit to world No 104 Yunchaokete Bu at the China Open on Friday.
metadata.content: China Open and Japan Open: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka all advance, as Katie Boulter knocked out | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content China Open and Japan Open: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka all advance, as Katie Boulter knocked out Novak Djokovic sealed a second-round comeback win in Beijing as Naomi Osaka and Aryna Sabalenka both advanced; Katie Boulter was once again beaten by Karolina Muchova watch ATP Japan Open and WTA/ATP China Open this week live on Sky Sports Friday 2 October 2026 19:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Djokovic extended his winning run at the China Open to 31 matches Novak Djokovic again appeared to struggle with fitness issues as he came from behind to avoid a second-round exit to world No 104 Yunchaokete Bu at the China Open on Friday. The Serbian went 1-0 down before he was taken to a tiebreak in the second set. But Djokovic dug deep to claim the final set and cap off a resilient 4-6 7-6(7-2) 6-2 comeback victory over the Chinese wildcard, and extend his record winning streak at the China Open to 31 matches.
